page: Amazon Web Services r5ad.24xlarge is a memory-optimized instance powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture with an AMD EPYC 7571 processor, delivering 96 virtual CPUs across 48 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading. The system is equipped with 768.0 GB of DDR4 memory operating at 3 GHz, providing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8 GB per vCPU. Local storage is bundled as 3600 GB of NVMe SSD instance store, and the baseline network bandwidth is rated at 20 Gbps.

Benchmark data reveals a clear contrast between single-core and multi-core capabilities. Single-core performance is relatively weak, with stress-ng, Geekbench, and single-threaded compression tests scoring in the bottom 10%. However, multi-core execution scales to average levels, as demonstrated by the Passmark CPU score and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression. Memory performance is a key strength, with cached small-block read bandwidth ranking in the top 25%, while uncached large-block read and write speeds remain average. Cryptographic operations also perform well, with the Passmark encryption test scoring in the top 25%.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the r5ad.24xlarge offers a dense allocation of DDR4 memory and fast local NVMe storage on AMD hardware, making it a viable alternative to more expensive Intel-based memory-optimized instances. The combination of 768 GB of RAM and 3.6 TB of local NVMe SSD makes this instance well-suited for memory-intensive workloads that require high-speed local scratch space. Appropriate workloads include large-scale databases, in-memory caching layers like Redis, big data analytics, and enterprise applications that benefit from high memory capacity but do not require top-tier single-core CPU performance.

It is best suited for large databases, in-memory caching, and data processing tasks that leverage high memory capacity and local NVMe storage rather than intensive single-threaded compute.
